answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. A velvet of per-task receipts records who did what, and the pulse of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, re-queued for a second panel, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. What survives to the hollow is a record of labour, not a list of addresses.
